{"type":"text","timestamp":1794692788583,"sessionID":"ses_e23fb11e7ffeVY6zv3FRBmSBAS","part":{"id":"prt_1dc06b15b001HkQGo5pT18fz2U","messageID":"msg_1dc0695c2001buRWXMTajVOSMm","sessionID":"ses_e23fb11e7ffeVY6zv3FRBmSBAS","type":"text","text":"I found and fixed four faults. All edge services were at 0% errors from minute 66 to the end of the shift at minute 120, with no throttles on and every scaled service back to its normal replica count.\n\n1. **audit-svc** (broke storefront and mobile, about 92% errors): deploy v44 changed a rate-limit refill calculation to divide by 1000. That set off a retry storm that kept the service overloaded. I scaled it from 3 to 9 replicas, rolled back v44, then scaled back to 3 once it was healthy.\n2. **limits-svc** (also storefront and mobile): config change cfg-21 cut the database pool size from 40 to 4. Reverting that config fixed it.\n3. **stock-svc** (partner-api at a steady 4%, about $760/min, the biggest loss): deploy v27 changed the price formatter so rows without a currency crash with `KeyError: 'currency'`. stock-svc's own metrics looked healthy; consent-svc's logs showed the errors. Since stock-svc was near capacity, I scaled it from 3 to 6 before rolling back v27, so the 30% failures during the rollback couldn't overload it. Then I scaled it back to 3.\n4. **checkout-svc** (new fault at minute 50, mobile-api at about 95%): config change cfg-52 set `entry_ttl_s` from 600 to 1, and the resulting errors caused another retry storm. I reverted the config and throttled checkout-svc to 70% for about 3 minutes to clear the backlog, then removed the throttle.\n\nNo mitigation went to a service that didn't need it. One thing I left alone: ranking-svc ran at about 98% CPU with about 1.3% errors, which cost storefront under $10/min. That was too small to justify a $10,000 risk on a wrong guess, and once stock-svc was fixed the storefront showed 0% errors.","time":{"start":1794692788571,"end":1794692788581}}}
